subject: ${^TAINT} is undef, not 0 — pre-existing value divergence (found by #237's probes)
description:
PROBED s382f (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL, plain code AND dq string — NOT introduced by #237's regex-interpolation wiring, only newly visible in patterns because `${^TAINT}` now interpolates there as perl does):

  my $t = ${^TAINT};  print "[", (defined $t ? $t : "UNDEF"), "]\n";
  print "dq=[${^TAINT}]\n";
    perl: [0]      dq=[0]
    PCL:  [UNDEF]  dq=[]

Cause: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp:835 `(defvar |${^TAINT}| nil "Taint mode is not enabled")` — a raw nil, and not a p-box like the other magic globals.

perl's contract: ${^TAINT} is 0 when taint checks are off, 1 when on, -1 with -t (warnings only). It is READ-ONLY. PCL never taints, so the constant is 0.

FIX (one line + a guard row): make it a p-box holding 0. Check the sibling magic globals for the boxing convention first (some magic scalars are raw values by design — verify which, since a box changes what `\${^TAINT}` and symbolic reads see). Guard row: a dq-string read (`"${^TAINT}"` eq "0") beside the existing magic-vars-01.t rows.

Not folded into the #237 commit: different mechanism (a runtime constant's value, not interpolation) — s366 filler rule.
